title: New native-only crate crates/apricity-link with the Link SDK binding; README row; build needs
description:
## Intent
Create the native-only crate that holds the Link peer, with the binding chosen in `design/link.md`.

## Steps
1. `crates/apricity-link/` (workspace member): `Cargo.toml` with the binding dependency decided in M0 (planned `rusty_link`), `license.workspace = true`; never built for wasm (the wasm build list and `apricity-web` don't depend on it).
2. README layout table: a row for `crates/apricity-link`.
3. Record the SDK's license and what it ships (GPL-2.0-or-later compatible on the desktop) in `design/link.md`; comment on apricitus-874f56 about iOS.
4. Note the build needs (cmake, a C++ compiler) in `docs/tools.md` "Getting set up" and on apricitus-1f0e91 for CI.

## Verify
`cargo build -p apricity-link` and `cargo build -p apricity-web --release --target wasm32-wasip1` (the wasm build must not pull the SDK); `cargo tree -p apricity-web | grep -c link` is 0.

Commit: `chore(<this task id>): apricity-link crate`.

## Protocol
Specs first, watched red; log decisions, problems and outcomes with `kbs comment`; run Verify and paste the tail. Every Bash call starts `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH && cd /Users/home/Projects/Apricity`; cargo with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` under `safe-run.sh --`. Never change dependencies to make a build pass. Sub-agents never commit, push or close.
